claims.proposition: Visible skill metadata can consume context or discovery budget.
claims.assessment: Anthropic documents always-visible discovery metadata with on-demand instructions. OpenAI documents a bounded Codex initial skill list with progressive disclosure and possible truncation or omission. These vendor-specific mechanisms support the distinction between metadata and full bodies; they do not quantify performance gains from deleting skills.
claims.limits: Vendor specifications are implementation-specific and mutable. Neither source establishes universal prompt overhead or a controlled deletion-versus-accuracy effect.

relationships.reason: Inspectability and retained evidence help distinguish repeatable agent work from impressive narrated outcomes. This is a methodological comparison, not proof that pruning skills improves agent accuracy.

An agent can retrieve and invoke a well-written skill without having authorization to change production systems. This comparison stresses accountable authority and observable action boundaries beyond instruction reuse.

Reducing discovery noise may save context, but removing rarely used tool knowledge can also impair incident response and capability recall. Both works support measuring accepted outcomes rather than rewarding file deletion.
